title: Computational Design of a Trivalent Multi-Epitope mRNA Vaccine Candidate Against Western, Eastern, and Venezuelan Equine Encephalitis Viruses.
authors: Qin, Rongliu; Luo, Yuying; Zhou, Ziyou; Xu, Yizhong; Wu, Xu; Hou, Yanqun; Chen, Jie; Zhu, Fei; Pan, Pinhua
one_liner_zh: 该文用免疫信息学与分子对接/MD模拟设计针对三种脑炎病毒的多表位mRNA疫苗，虽涉及蛋白结构预测与模拟，但核心对象是疫苗抗原表位而非蛋白质结构计算问题，方法偏应用且无结构建模创新。
abstract: PURPOSE: Western equine encephalitis virus (WEEV), Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV), and Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV) are mosquito-borne neurotropic alphaviruses that can cause severe encephalitis in humans and equids, yet no licensed vaccines are currently available for routine human prevention. This study aimed to computationally design a trivalent multi-epitope mRNA vaccine targeting WEEV, EEEV, and VEEV. METHODS: Immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology approaches were used to identify conserved cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and linear B-cell epitopes from the three viruses. Fifteen candidate constructs incorporating different immunomodulatory strategies were evaluated for predicted antigenicity, safety, stability, and solubility, and the construct with the most balanced overall profile was selected for further analysis. Secondary- and tertiary-structure prediction, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, binding free-energy analysis, and immune simulation were subsequently performed. RESULTS: WEV showed a favorable overall physicochemical and immunological profile, supporting its further structural and immunological characterization. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable interactions between WEV and TLR2, TLR3, and TLR4, with the strongest predicted HADDOCK score observed for TLR4. In contrast, molecular dynamics simulations and MM-PBSA analysis indicated greater dynamic stability and a more favorable estimated binding free energy for the WEV-TLR2 complex. In silico immune simulation predicted enhanced IgM and IgG production, B- and T-cell responses, memory-cell formation, and increased IFN-gamma and IL-2 levels. CONCLUSIONS: WEV represents a computationally designed trivalent multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidate against WEEV, EEEV, and VEEV. The present study provides a sequence-defined framework for the rational development of multivalent vaccines, and further in vitro and in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate antigen expression, immunogenicity, protective efficacy, and safety.
abstract_zh: 目的：西方马脑炎病毒（WEEV）、东方马脑炎病毒（EEEV）和委内瑞拉马脑炎病毒（VEEV）是蚊媒嗜神经性甲病毒，可在人类和奇蹄类动物中引起严重脑炎，但目前尚无许可疫苗用于常规人类预防。本研究旨在通过计算设计一种针对WEEV、EEEV和VEEV的三价多表位mRNA疫苗。方法：采用免疫信息学和反向疫苗学方法，从三种病毒中鉴定保守的细胞毒性T淋巴细胞、辅助性T淋巴细胞和线性B细胞表位。评估了十五种包含不同免疫调节策略的候选构建体的预测抗原性、安全性、稳定性和可溶性，并选择总体特征最均衡的构建体进行进一步分析。随后进行了二级和三级结构预测、分子对接、分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟、结合自由能分析和免疫模拟。结果：WEV显示出良好的总体理化及免疫学特征，支持其进一步的结构和免疫学表征。分子对接表明WEV与TLR2、TLR3和TLR4之间存在有利相互作用，其中TLR4的预测HADDOCK评分最强。相比之下，分子动力学模拟和MM-PBSA分析表明，WEV-TLR2复合物具有更高的动态稳定性和更有利的估计结合自由能。计算机免疫模拟预测了IgM和IgG产生增强、B细胞和T细胞反应、记忆细胞形成以及IFN-γ和IL-2水平升高。结论：WEV代表了一种针对WEEV、EEEV和VEEV的计算设计三价多表位mRNA疫苗候选物。本研究为多价疫苗的合理开发提供了序列定义的框架，未来需进一步开展体外和体内研究以评估抗原表达、免疫原性、保护效力和安全性。
